gen-fs-quilon-gf-noto-sans-osage: Quilon's strokes swell and thin in a slow, steady ebb. Noto Sans Osage sits beneath it as a plain sans, its rounded bowls filling the line while the curves stay wide open.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-noto-sans-osmanya: Quilon bends its strokes with a faint taper at every turn, which gives headings an editorial edge. And Noto Sans Osmanya carries the text with wide, easy s shapes, so a long page feels unhurried and clear.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-noto-sans-pahawh-hmong: Thick, confident strokes that guide the eye. Quilon leads with that weight while Noto Sans Pahawh Hmong stays lighter and contemporary beneath it, its tall x-height keeping the two comfortable side by side without any tug of war.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-noto-sans-palmyrene: Quilon shades its round and straight strokes by a moderate amount, giving each heading a measured, editorial presence. Noto Sans Palmyrene then reads cleanly as a plain sans, its curves stopping short.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-noto-sans-pau-cin-hau: Noto Sans Pau Cin Hau brings open-ended curves and capitals only a short step above its lowercase, giving the text a modern feel. Quilon above it thickens and thins in gentle steps.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-noto-sans-phagspa: Commanding in tone, Quilon tapers gently wherever its strokes bend and turn. Noto Sans PhagsPa lowers the temperature as a sans-serif with see-through openings, and capitals that rise only a little, so the two feel like a firm voice and a friendly one.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-noto-sans-phoenician: Editorial poise with a lightly modulated stroke. But Noto Sans Phoenician has the other job, with s curves opening wide at both ends and generous lowercase height, while Quilon handles the headline voice.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-noto-sans-psalter-pahla: Sharp, editorial, and a touch lighter across the horizontals. Noto Sans Psalter Pahlavi follows as a sans-serif with gaping e shapes and barely rising capitals, so extended text feels approachable and easy to settle into.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-noto-sans-rejang: Thin strokes that still carry real weight. Noto Sans Rejang takes over for the text with lowercase counters like wide portholes, so a long passage looks open and steady from line to line.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-noto-sans-runic: Quilon opens the page with an editorial, commanding stroke that moves between thick and thin in moderation. Noto Sans Runic follows as a sans with a big x-height, its curves never closing back on themselves.
